To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

severely and profoundly mentally handicapped adults spend most of their time in ordinary housing doing purposeful activity and that the majority of their time is spent in domestic or household activities.
the people we studied spent between 22% and 67% (median 44%) of their available time in purposeless activity, and between 27% and 65% (median 50%) of their purposeful activity in domestic tasks.

severely and profoundly mentally handicapped adults in ordinary settings spend between 22% and 67% (mean 47.6%) of available time engaged in purposeful activity and that between 27% and 65% (mean 48.6%) of purposeful activity is engaged in domestic and housework tasks.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a methodology for assessing the quality of care for severely and profoundly handicapped adults in ordinary community settings.
the question of whether it is possible to measure the quality of care of severely and profoundly handicapped adults. (PsycINFO Database Record (c) 2012 APA, all rights reserved)
the quality of life of people who are severely and profoundly mentally handicapped, and the quality of care provided by staff.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the quality of life of severely and profoundly handicapped people in ordinary housing is very good indeed.
there is no evidence that the use of recreational materials in ordinary housing is either necessary or sufficient to promote purposeful engagement.

the data are consistent with a view that the use of simple materials to promote engagement in domestic tasks is a valuable use of time and that it is important to continue to explore ways to extend the range of domestic tasks in which Ss can participate. (Author/JAC)
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, in the absence of a well-developed system of support, the quality of care for severely and profoundly disabled adults in ordinary housing can only be improved by a more extensive use of simple, recreational materials to occupy the time of those with severe and profound disabilities.
the quality of care provided by staffed houses for the severely mentally-handicapped is generally good, although it is not as good as it might be.
the use of simple recreational material to engage people in purposeful activity is not justified. (PsycINFO Database Record (c) 2006 APA, all rights reserved)
The main takeaway from our work is that
the majority of severely and profoundly handicapped adults spend the majority of their time engaged in domestic and household tasks.
the quality of life of severely and profoundly handicapped adults can be enhanced by providing opportunities for purposeful and meaningful activity in ordinary housing.
it is possible to measure the activity of profoundly handicapped adults in their own homes and that this is an essential prerequisite to evaluating the effects of different forms of care.
